meta.title: Somali Alphabet
meta.subtitle: 33 letters and sounds · both directions, as two cards per letter
meta.desc: The Latin alphabet in which Somali has been written since 1972: 33 notes — the 21 consonants in the order Somali primers give them (b t j x kh d r s sh dh c g f q k l m n w h y), the glottal stop written with an apostrophe, the five vowels, the long vowels, and five diphthongs. The first deck of the Somali collection. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Most of the letters sound as an English reader expects, and the cards say so in a line; the notes that matter are the ones English reads otherwise — X, a breathy h from deep in the throat, and C, the voiced throat sound of the Arabic ʿayn (neither is the English letter's sound); DH, a d with the tongue curled back; Q, a k at the very back of the mouth; KH, the ch of loch; the apostrophe, which is a consonant; and the doubled vowels, which are long. Each card gives one everyday word that shows the sound, from the Somali A1 deck, with, where English Wiktionary gives it, the same word with its accent (the high tone) marked — a mark ordinary writing leaves out. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them, for Standard Somali. There is no read-aloud button: few devices carry a Somali voice, and one without it reads the letter in English. Sources: the standard description of Standard Somali; the example words' accents are English Wiktionary's, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0).

always the hard g of go — never the g of gem
